messages:
julie-support: Heads up — tenant HyperLogix reporting a bunch of 429s on /v1/chat/streaming starting ~07:20 UTC. They say average is ~20 r/s but bursts push it to ~280 r/s near minute boundaries. Users also see high tail latency. Sample response below.

maria-ops: Can you paste the exact response headers (one full example) + a correlation id? Also which region/route and SDK version?

julie-support: Region eu-west-1, route /v1/chat/streaming, SDK js-client v1.4.2. Correlation: 01H7X3Z9QK. Response headers we captured: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
`content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8`
`x-request-id: 01H7X3Z9QK`
`x-rate-limit-limit-rpm: 800`
`x-rate-limit-remaining-rpm: 0`
`x-rate-limit-reset: 1747256820`
`retry-after: 3`
Body: `\{"error":"rate_limited","code":"rate_limit","retry_after":3}`

sam-runtime: Those headers imply a per-tenant RPM cap is being hit (800rpm). If they've only got ~20 r/s steady-state that shouldn't happen unless traffic is highly bursty or multiple clients share the same token. Do they use connection multiplexing / many parallel streams?

julie-support: Customer says they have a fleet of workers that all run a sync job at top of minute (cron-ish). Each worker opens 6 streams and does short conversations. They also use HTTP/2 from server-side env.

nate-platform: That pattern will stack. If 50 workers x 6 streams -> 300 concurrent starts at the same second, you get huge per-minute buckets. We should ask them to run a quick aggregation on our logs. Suggested query (copy/paste for logs UI):
`SELECT toStartOfMinute(timestamp) AS minute, count() AS requests FROM requests_raw WHERE tenant = 'hyperlogix' AND timestamp >= now() - interval 10 minute GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute DESC LIMIT 10;`

ryan-oncall: I ran that for the last 10m: most minutes are ~600-900 reqs but every top-of-minute minute spikes to 1500-2400. Confirmed correlation with an internal cron we identified (worker-launch-ts). This explains 429s.

maria-ops: Short-term mitigation options:
- Ask customer to add jitter to cron (5-30s) and randomize start times :clock8:.
- Advise exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s (base 100ms, cap 5s).
- If they need immediate relief, we can temporarily increase the tenant burst window for this route.

sam-runtime: Operational notes: our per-tenant limiter enforces both RPM and concurrent-token windows. If high concurrency + minute-aligned bursts happen, RPM resets at the minute boundary but many requests fall into the prior minute window and still count. Also HTTP/2 multiplexing can make many logical requests hit the token at once when they all flush frames. Recommend reducing concurrent stream count to ~8-10 per connection.

julie-support: Customer asked for step-by-step repro we can send them. Drafted repro: `1) spawn N workers (we used 50) 2) have each worker open 6 streams 3) schedule all to start at t=0 (top of minute) 4) observe >=x429s and headers above`. Ok to send?

nate-platform: Yes, include curl example for deterministic repro: `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-4r","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' https://eu-west-1.api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/streaming` and run that concurrently with a small harness. Also include note to capture `x-rate-limit-*` headers.

maria-ops: Temporary action we took: increased tenant soft-burst for /v1/chat/streaming to +200rpm until 1747258200 and added a dashboard watch. opsbot: please add an incident note and monitor an alert for x-rate-limit-remaining-rpm==0 for hyperlogix.

opsbot: Incident note added: INC-2024-3872 — soft-burst applied to tenant=hyperlogix route=/v1/chat/streaming until 1747258200. Alert rule created: alert if x-rate-limit-remaining-rpm == 0 for 3 consecutive minutes.

ryan-oncall: Customer notified with mitigations (jitter/backoff) and repro steps. Ask them to rollout changes and re-open if 429s persist after spreading starts. :thumbsup:

julie-support: Thanks team — will follow up with the customer and include our recommended client changes + repro harness. If they ask for a permanent quota bump, direct to acct team for reserved capacity conversation.
